D.treatment: repetitive practice with anodal tDCS at left PMd

O.outcome_detail: total time on the motor-sequence test immediately after practice

cells.quote: Subsequent post-hoc assessment of the performance during the IMM test revealed that individuals that received anodal stimulation at left PMd ( M = 1556 ms, SEM = 60 ms) and right PMd ( M = 1551 ms, SEM = 42 ms) did not differ ( p = 0.96), but mean TT for both stimulation conditions were signiﬁcantly lower than mean TT for the individuals assigned to the RP-Sham ( M = 1909 ms, SEM = 78 ms) and IP-Sham ( M = 1949 ms, SEM = 59 ms) conditions ( p < 0.001).
cells.note: The reported effect size is for the omnibus condition effect; the post-hoc comparison supports the treatment direction.

O.outcome_detail: change in total time from immediate to 6-hour post-practice test

cells.quote: Speci ﬁcally, post hoc assessment revealed that the change in TT from the immediate to 6-h test was similar for R-PMd, L-PMd, and the RP-S conditions but differed from the IP-S condition which was the only condition that exhibited an improvement in performance after only 6-hrs post-practice (Fig. 1E).
cells.note: The 6-hour assessment does not fit the provided immediate or day-or-more delayed timing categories.
